name: Primary Surveillance Radar
summary: Finds aircraft by bouncing radio pulses off them, with no help from the aircraft.

name: Secondary Surveillance Radar and Mode S
summary: Asks each aircraft "who are you and how high?" and reads the answer.

name: ADS-B and ADS-C
summary: Aircraft broadcast their own satellite position twice a second.

name: Multilateration (MLAT and WAM)
summary: Pinpoints an aircraft from tiny differences in when its signal arrives.

name: Surface Movement Radar and A-SMGCS
summary: A live map of every aircraft and vehicle on the airport, even in fog.

name: NDB and ADF
summary: A beacon that sends the same signal everywhere; the needle points at it.

name: VOR (Conventional and Doppler)
summary: Two signals ticking out of step tell you your direction from the station.

name: Distance Measuring Equipment
summary: Ask the ground "how far?", time the answer, and get the distance.

name: Instrument Landing System
summary: Two radio beams guide the aircraft down to the runway in fog.

name: GNSS with SBAS and GBAS
summary: Satellites broadcast the exact time; the receiver works out where it is.

name: VHF and UHF Air-Ground Radio
summary: Press to talk: straight-line radio whose range depends on height.

name: HF Radio
summary: Radio waves that bounce off the sky to reach across oceans.

name: Controller–Pilot Data Link (CPDLC)
summary: Standard text messages instead of crowded voice radio.

name: Satellite Communication (SATCOM)
summary: Talking to ATC through satellites over oceans and poles.

name: Airspace Sandbox
summary: One flight, gate to gate: every system at work, and what happens when one fails.
